slides.title: Did Valmiki mention *diyas*?
slides.sub: Dadi said Ayodhya lit diyas for Rama. The 8-year-old asked: "Valmiki ne likha hai?" Let's check.

slides.title: The question at *Diwali dinner*
slides.body: Dadi: "Ayodhya lit diyas when Rama came home." Little Tara: "Did Valmiki write that?" The table went quiet. So we opened the Ramayana.

slides.title: Rama sends *Hanuman ahead*
slides.body: The text says Rama asks Hanuman to watch Bharata's face when he hears the news. If Bharata wants to stay king, let him.

slides.title: Bharata says: *get the city ready*
slides.body: Bharata is overjoyed. He tells his brother Shatrughna: worship in every temple, bring music and flowers, and let everyone come out to see Rama.

slides.deva: समुच्छ्रितपताकास्तु रथ्याः पुरवरोत्तमे । शोभयन्तु च वेश्मानि सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति ॥
slides.iast: samucchrita-patākās tu rathyāḥ puravarottame, śobhayantu ca veśmāni sūryasyodayanaṃ prati
slides.meaning: Raise tall flags on the streets of this great city, and decorate every house before sunrise.

slides.title: So, where are the *diyas*?
slides.body: The text says: flags, flowers, cool water on the roads, music, crowds. This welcome names no lamps. Tradition holds the diyas, and Diwali keeps them.

slides.title: Dadi and Valmiki *both* win
slides.body: For us today: Valmiki gives the welcome, Dadi gives the diya. Same message: when someone you love comes home, make the house shine.

slides.title: Save it. *Send it* to the family group.
slides.sub: Next time someone asks "Valmiki ne likha hai?", you'll have the verse ready. Follow @sutraverselife for real-life lessons from ancient wisdom.
